AI disclosure

AI coding assistants helped build this site. Here is which models were used, how I reviewed and iterated on every output, and where the boundary sits.

Models used

Two model families were used as coding and editing assistants while building and hosting this site:

  • Claude (Anthropic): initial static site generator, candidate ledger extraction from local repositories and notes, and visual restyling.
  • Gemini (Google): EndeavourOS Beelink hosting setup, container and deployment fixes, and follow-up site edits.

Where AI helped

AI coding assistants were used as build and editing tools for the site itself:

  • Static site generator: drafting and iterating on build.py, portfolio/render.py, portfolio/validate.py, CSS layout, and verify/verify.py.
  • Ledger assembly: extracting candidate entries, commit hashes, and file paths from local repositories and notes into content/ledger.yaml for review.
  • Hosting and deployment: writing Docker, Caddy, Cloudflare Tunnel, systemd, and GitHub Actions configs under infra/ and .github/workflows/.
  • Prose drafting: initial wording for navigation, layout copy, and repository documentation.

Review and iteration

No generated output went live unreviewed. I checked each page, wording pass, and ledger entry myself and iterated through many rounds of revision before publishing.

Earlier passes were discarded or reworked when the visual style looked generic, when narrow screens overflowed, when prose overstated what the evidence supported, or when hosting configs failed live checks. Every revision still had to pass the validator test suite, deterministic build, and verification script before deploying.

What AI does not decide

The factual record and publication gates do not rest on model output:

  • Build-time checks: every claim renders from content/ledger.yaml and is checked deterministically by build.py and verify/verify.py. A MEASURED entry fails the build without explicit metrics, denominators, datasets, and evidence pointers; a LINKED entry requires a file path, branch, and commit SHA.
  • Visible uncertainty: unverified statements are labeled AUTHOR-REPORTED, STALE (older than 90 days), or UNKNOWN rather than filled in with generated prose.
  • Author direction: I chose the visual direction, scope, which entries are public or hidden, and what gets published.

Why state this here

My work is about AI verification and grounding: systems where a model may propose, but a deterministic check decides what gets admitted.

Applying that same rule to the portfolio means stating plainly which models assisted, how their output was reviewed across iterations, and letting the ledger, commit hashes, and build checks carry the evidence instead of prose.

Built 2026-11-25 from content/ledger.yaml. STALE = as_of older than 90 days at build time. Machine-readable: ledger.json · Resume · AI disclosure.
